papers.title_in_file: A resource theory of asynchronous quantum information processing
papers.what_it_is: A quantum information theory paper that defines a hierarchy of port-based teleportation resource theories (PBT, PBTcl, PBTq, PBTmax), computes their teleportation fidelities for isotropic, graph and symmetrized EPR states, and shows PBTmax is as strong as one-way LOCC for beating the classical threshold.

quotes: On the other hand, since PBTmax is sufficiently strong to break the classical threshold for two-qubit states, it is an interesting open problem to identify the minimal type of pre-processing beyond PBTq needed for non-classical teleportation of two-qubit states.
existing.certainty_reason: The Conclusion states the open problem in the authors' own words.

existing.note: The abstract's 'trivial decoding map of discarding subsystems' is the PBTmax model, which also lets Bob apply an arbitrary local pre-processing map before Alice's message. The result is Corollary 18, whose statement is now quoted; the narrower value names the pre-processing.
existing.value: The paper proves (Corollary 18) that a bipartite state can generate a teleportation channel whose fidelity exceeds the classical threshold by one-way LOCC if and only if it can also do so using PBTmax, in which Bob may apply arbitrary local pre-processing before Alice's classical message and, after the message, can only discard subsystems.

quotes: Corollary 18. A bipartite state ρAB can generate a |C|- dimensional teleportation channel whose fidelity exceeds 1 |C| by one-way LOCC if and only if it can also generate such a channel using PBTmax.
(v) Arbitrary local pre-processing by Bob prior to him receiving Alice's classical communication.
The only action that Bob can perform conditioned on Alice's message is a trivial discarding of subsystems.
Hence, interactive local quantum processing is not necessary to realize the one-way teleportation capability of any bipartite state.

assertions.value: The paper defines standard PBT as the quantum resource theory whose free operations are arbitrary local quantum operations by Alice, classical communication from Alice to Bob, and relabeling and discarding of subsystems by Bob.
quotes: (i) Arbitrary local quantum operations by Alice; (ii) Classical communication from Alice to Bob; (iii) Relabeling and discarding of subsystems by Bob. When limited to these three types of action, we refer to the QRT as standard PBT.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III A 1 gives the definition.

assertions.value: The paper defines PBTcl as standard PBT plus the free preparation of classical states by Bob, and shows that a PBTcl channel can be simulated by Bob first preparing d additional ports in classical basis states, independent of the shared state.
quotes: (iv) Preparation of classical states by Bob. We denote this resource-theoretic QRT by PBTcl

assertions.value: The paper defines maximal PBT (PBTmax) as allowing arbitrary local pre-processing by Bob before he receives Alice's classical communication, with the restriction that the pre-processing cannot depend on Alice's message and that the only action conditioned on her message is discarding subsystems.
quotes: (v) Arbitrary local pre-processing by Bob prior to him receiving Alice's classical communication.
The key restriction in (v) is that Bob's choice of local pre-processing map cannot depend on Alice's message.
We refer to this operational setting as maximal PBT, denoted by PBTmax, since it captures the most general physical processes feasible under the constraint of trivial post-processing for Bob.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III A 3 gives the definition.

assertions.value: The paper defines PBTq as the PBT protocols in which Bob's pre-processing is restricted to preparing additional ports in arbitrary states independent of Alice's input, and the authors state that its physical motivation is less clear.
quotes: (iv') Preparation of arbitrary states by Bob. In other words, PBTq consists of all PBT protocols for which Bob's pre-processing is restricted to just preparing additional ports in arbitrary states that are independent of Alice's input.
The physical motivation for studying the resource theory of PBTq is less clear

papers.what_it_is: An engineering quantum-computing paper that proposes a two-register variational quantum algorithm for constrained topology optimization, analyzes its gate complexity, bounds volume-constraint violation, and demonstrates it on three trusses and two MBB beams in a noiseless Qiskit simulator.

quotes: The proposed VQA is demonstrated with compliance minimization problems involving three truss structures and two MBB beams.
Across all five examples, the VQA is implemented with at most 12 qubits and 22 Hermitian operators in the problem Hamiltonian.
existing.certainty_reason: Section 5 states the size of the demonstrations.

existing.value: The authors state that the number of gates scales with a factor of order v squared times a squared logarithm of the largest entry of the operator times poly(n), where v is the maximum number of elements connected to a node and n the number of qubits; this factor depends on the sparsity of the stiffness matrices, the degree of element connectivity and the number of qubits, and since the stiffness matrices are typically sparse and connectivity small for two- and three-dimensional structures, the number of gates scales polynomially in the number of qubits.
